Project Summary


Our project addresses the NASA Space Apps Challenge: Flame in Freefall by building an interactive, AI-powered dashboard designed to interpret and summarize decades of microgravity combustion data. In free fall, fire behaves unpredictably due to the absence of buoyancy-driven convection, turning into a spherical shape where flame spread, ignition, and extinguishment change drastically compared to Earth. To make this complex volume of research actionable for future lunar and Martian habitats, our platform compiles, ranks, and visualizes raw experimental log files and scientific insights to support crew fire safety.
details:
What It Does

  • Data Processing & AI Analysis: Utilizes machine learning models to automatically summarize and categorize extensive microgravity combustion datasets (such as BASS-II or Saffire) from NASA's Physical Science Informatics (PSI) repository.
  • Interactive Dashboard: Provides a user-friendly panel to filter and compare missions based on atmospheric pressure, fuel type, and oxygen concentrations.
  • Safety Insights & Ranking: Ranks flammability limits and materials according to risk factors to deliver data-driven fire safety guidelines for human space exploration.

  • Data & Analytics: Leveraged [e.g., Python / Pandas / Jupyter Notebooks] to clean and filter the PSI open data records.
  • AI/Intelligence integration: Integrated [e.g., OpenAI API / Hugging Face models / Custom LLM agents] to translate complex text logs into structured safety summaries.
  • Visualization: Powered by [e.g., Three.js / D3.js / Plotly] to render data patterns and flame models.
